vo.sub: In this video, we'll install OpenCrabs on Ubuntu with a single paste, from zero to your first chat.
You need Ubuntu 24.04 or newer on a 64-bit machine, an internet connection, and a key or subscription from an AI provider.
Open a terminal. On the Ubuntu desktop, press Control, Alt and T.
First, one quick check. Your glibc version must be 2.39 or newer.
Here it says 2.39, so we're good. Older than that? This download won't run there, so watch the older systems video instead.
Now the whole install is one paste. Copy this block from the docs or the description, paste it into the terminal, and press Enter.
On an ARM machine, copy the arm64 block from the docs instead. It's the same, with arm64 in the file name.
Ubuntu asks for your password. Nothing appears while you type it. That's normal. Type it and press Enter.
Then it does everything in one go. It installs three small helpers, finds the newest release, downloads it, and starts OpenCrabs.
The setup wizard opens. Choose QuickStart, the sensible defaults, and press Enter.

Home Base is the dot opencrabs folder in your home directory. That's always the default. Keep Seed template files ticked. We recommend it: those files give your crab its personality, so you start with the complete crab. You can change them later if you want. Press Enter.
Brain Fuel is the important one. Pick your AI provider. We'll choose Anthropic.
Now paste your API key, or a setup token if you have a Claude subscription. It's hidden on screen. Never share your key with anyone.
Keep the default model, or pick another one, and press Enter.
Always On can keep OpenCrabs running in the background. Skip it for now. There's a separate video for that.
Vibe Check makes sure everything is wired up. All OK? Press Enter.
Make It Yours lets you tell OpenCrabs about yourself. Press Escape to skip it for now.
Setup complete. And you're in. Say hi.
It answers. Your reply will be different, but that's it. OpenCrabs is installed and running.
Next time, start it the same way. Open a terminal in your home folder, type ./opencrabs and press Enter.
If something goes wrong, here are the three errors people hit most, and the fix for each.
GLIBC_2.39 not found means your system is too old for this download. Watch the older systems video instead.
libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file means the helpers are missing. Paste the install block again.
gzip: unexpected end of file means the version lookup came back empty. Wait a moment, then paste the block again.
Every command from this video is in the description, ready to copy.
Next up: keep OpenCrabs running in the background, and connect it to Telegram so you can chat from your phone. See you there.
